title: Admin layout renders persistent navigation
description: The admin frontend module shall render a persistent navigation bar with links to Users, Audit Log, Config, and Courses views.
rationale: Admins need a consistent top-level entry point to all admin views without reloading the application.

title: Admin routes enforce admin role
description: The admin frontend module shall redirect any authenticated non-admin user who navigates to an admin route to /dashboard.
rationale: Student accounts must never access admin views; a client-side guard prevents accidental exposure before the backend rejects the request.

title: User management view
description: The admin frontend module shall provide a user lifecycle management view.
rationale: Administrators must be able to manage the full user lifecycle from a single view.

title: Audit log view
description: The admin frontend module shall provide a paginated view of audit log entries with an integrity verification action.
rationale: Administrators must be able to review all system actions and confirm the hash-chain has not been tampered with.

title: System config view
description: The admin frontend module shall provide a form for viewing and patching all thirteen system configuration keys.
rationale: System configuration controls runtime behaviour of grading, sessions, and content generation; admins need a safe form interface with validation feedback.

title: Course oversight view
description: The admin frontend module shall provide a read-only paginated view of all courses with status filtering.
rationale: Admins need system-wide course visibility to monitor enrolments and diagnose pipeline issues without the ability to mutate course state.

title: Admin nav displays current username
description: The admin frontend module shall display the authenticated admin's username in the navigation bar.
rationale: Multi-admin environments require the current operator to know which account they are acting under.

title: Admin views show loading state during fetch
description: The admin frontend module shall display a loading indicator while any data retrieval operation is in progress.
rationale: Network latency must not leave the admin with a blank or stale view; a visible indicator prevents duplicate actions.

title: Admin views surface network errors
description: The admin frontend module shall display an error banner when any API call returns a network or server error.
rationale: Silent failures leave admins unaware that their action had no effect; a visible error banner prompts a retry.

title: Nav link — Users
description: The admin frontend module shall render a Users navigation link that routes to /admin/users.
rationale: Admin users need frequent access to user management without navigating through intermediary pages.

title: Nav link — Audit Log
description: The admin frontend module shall render an Audit Log navigation link that routes to /admin/audit.
rationale: Admins must be able to review and verify the tamper-evident audit trail at any time to meet oversight obligations.

title: Nav link — Config
description: The admin frontend module shall render a Config navigation link that routes to /admin/config.
rationale: System configuration directly affects grading and agent behaviour; admins need direct access to adjust it without friction.

title: Nav link — Courses
description: The admin frontend module shall render a Courses navigation link that routes to /admin/courses.
rationale: Admins need visibility into all student courses system-wide to support quality assurance and student assistance.

title: Redirect unauthenticated user from admin routes
description: The admin frontend module shall redirect an unauthenticated visitor who navigates to any /admin route to /login.
rationale: Unauthenticated users must never reach admin views.

title: Redirect student from admin routes
description: The admin frontend module shall redirect an authenticated student who navigates to any /admin route to /dashboard.
rationale: Students must be returned to their own dashboard instead of receiving an error page.

title: Nav bar displays admin username
description: The admin frontend module shall read the username from the auth session store and render it in the navigation bar.
rationale: The username must come from local session state, not a separate API call, to avoid latency on every page load.

title: Loading indicator during in-flight requests
description: The admin frontend module shall render a loading spinner in place of list content while data retrieval is pending.
rationale: Users must receive visual feedback that data is loading rather than seeing an empty list.

title: Error banner on API failure
description: The admin frontend module shall display a dismissible error banner with the server error message on any HTTP 500 response.
rationale: Server errors must be surfaced so admins can retry or report the issue.

title: User list fetches all users
description: The admin frontend module shall retrieve all system users on mount and render one row per user.
rationale: The user management view requires a complete user list to perform management actions. Note: the GET /api/v1/users backend endpoint is being added in Sprint 5 T7 to support this view.

title: Create user modal
description: The admin frontend module shall open a user creation modal when the Create User button is clicked.
rationale: User creation requires a dedicated form to capture all required fields without navigating away from the list.

title: Edit user modal
description: The admin frontend module shall open an edit modal populated with the existing username and email when Edit is clicked.
rationale: Editing must show existing values so the admin only changes what is needed.

title: Deactivate user action
description: The admin frontend module shall confirm then submit the user deactivation when Deactivate is clicked on an active user.
rationale: Deactivation is destructive to the user's session; a confirmation step prevents accidental deactivation.

title: Activate user action
description: The admin frontend module shall submit the user activation when Activate is clicked on an inactive user.
rationale: Reactivation restores login access; the list must immediately reflect the change.

title: Delete student action
description: The admin frontend module shall require confirmation before permanently deleting a student account.
rationale: Deletion is irreversible and removes all student data; a confirmation step with a specific warning prevents accidental deletion.

title: Delete button visible only for student users
description: The admin frontend module shall render the Delete button only on rows where the user's role is student.
rationale: The backend rejects deletion of non-student accounts; hiding the button prevents invalid requests and reduces admin confusion.

title: Deactivate button visible only for active users
description: The admin frontend module shall render the Deactivate button only on rows where the user is active.
rationale: Showing only the applicable action reduces cognitive load and prevents sending an invalid deactivation request for an already-inactive user.

title: Activate button visible only for inactive users
description: The admin frontend module shall render the Activate button only on rows where the user is inactive.
rationale: Showing only the applicable action reduces cognitive load and prevents sending an invalid activation request for an already-active user.

title: Audit log initial load
description: The admin frontend module shall retrieve the audit log entries on mount and render each returned entry.
rationale: The audit view must start with the most recent entries using the server default page size of 50.

title: Audit log pagination
description: The admin frontend module shall append older audit entries on Load More using the next_before cursor from the prior response.
rationale: The full audit log can be very large; cursor-based pagination loads only what is needed.

title: Audit log entry display fields
description: The admin frontend module shall display admin_id, action, target_type, target_id, created_at, and a truncated entry_hash for each audit entry.
rationale: These are the fields returned by GET /api/v1/audit and are sufficient for an admin to identify the actor, action, and target.

title: Audit log integrity verification
description: The admin frontend module shall request audit log integrity verification and display the outcome when Verify Integrity is clicked.
rationale: Integrity verification must be a manual admin action to avoid flooding the server with streaming verification on every page load.

title: Config view fetches all keys on mount
description: The admin frontend module shall retrieve the current system configuration on mount and populate all thirteen form fields.
rationale: All config keys must be loaded before the admin edits any value to prevent overwriting fields with stale or empty data.

title: Config save issues PATCH with changed keys only
description: The admin frontend module shall submit the updated configuration with only changed keys when Save is clicked.
rationale: Sending unchanged keys wastes bandwidth and triggers unnecessary audit entries for config.change.

title: Config unsaved changes indicator
description: The admin frontend module shall display You have unsaved changes. when any config field value differs from its fetched value.
rationale: Admins who navigate away from the config view after editing without saving lose their changes silently; the indicator prevents this.

title: Config field-level client-side validation
description: The admin frontend module shall display per-field validation errors before submit when any config value violates its defined constraint.
rationale: Client-side validation prevents a round-trip to the server for obviously invalid values and gives immediate feedback.

title: Config save success banner
description: The admin frontend module shall display a Configuration saved. banner when the configuration update succeeds.
rationale: Admins need positive confirmation that the save succeeded because the form stays visible after saving.

title: Config save server validation error display
description: The admin frontend module shall display server-returned validation errors as per-field messages when the configuration update is rejected.
rationale: The server enforces cross-field rules such as weight sum that cannot be fully validated on the client; these errors must be shown against the correct fields.

title: Course oversight list fetches all courses
description: The admin frontend module shall retrieve all courses in the system on mount and display each returned course.
rationale: Admin users receive all courses system-wide from the listCourses handler when no student filter is applied.

title: Course oversight status filter
description: The admin frontend module shall retrieve all courses filtered by the selected status when the status dropdown value changes.
rationale: Admins monitoring a specific pipeline stage need to narrow the list without scrolling through all courses.

title: Course oversight row fields
description: The admin frontend module shall display student_id, topic, status, and created_at for each course row.
rationale: These four fields give the admin enough information to identify the student, subject, current state, and age of the course.

title: Course oversight pagination
description: The admin frontend module shall retrieve and append the next course page on Load More using the prior response's next_cursor.
rationale: System-wide course lists can be very large; cursor pagination avoids loading all rows at once.

title: GET /api/v1/users request
description: The admin frontend module shall send GET /api/v1/users with the Authorization header on user list mount.
rationale: All authenticated admin endpoints require a valid session cookie and CSRF token.

title: User list row — username column
description: The admin frontend module shall render the username field from each user object in a dedicated table column.
rationale: Username is the primary human-readable identifier for each account.

title: User list row — role and status columns
description: The admin frontend module shall render the role and is_active fields from each user object in dedicated table columns.
rationale: Role and active status determine which action buttons appear for each row.

title: User list row — created_at column
description: The admin frontend module shall render the created_at field from each user object formatted as a local date-time string.
rationale: Account age is useful context when reviewing the user list.

title: Create user modal — username field required
description: The admin frontend module shall show Username is required. and block submission when the username field is empty.
rationale: The POST /api/v1/users handler returns HTTP 400 for a missing username; client-side validation avoids the round-trip.

title: Create user modal — role field required
description: The admin frontend module shall show Role is required. and block submission when no role is selected.
rationale: The POST /api/v1/users handler returns HTTP 400 for a missing role; client-side validation avoids the round-trip.

title: Create user modal — password field required
description: The admin frontend module shall show Password is required. and block submission when the password field is empty.
rationale: The POST /api/v1/users handler returns HTTP 400 for a missing password; client-side validation avoids the round-trip.

title: Create user modal — role dropdown options
description: The admin frontend module shall offer exactly two options in the role dropdown: student and admin.
rationale: The backend accepts only the string values student and admin for the role field.

title: Create user modal — POST request body
description: The admin frontend module shall send POST /api/v1/users with JSON body containing username, email, role, and password fields.
rationale: The createUser handler decodes exactly these four fields; extra or renamed fields are ignored or cause errors.

title: Create user modal — email is optional
description: The admin frontend module shall omit the email key from the POST body when the email field is empty.
rationale: The handler treats a missing email key differently from an empty string; an absent key maps to a nil pointer, preserving null in the database.

title: Create user — HTTP 201 success handling
description: The admin frontend module shall close the modal and prepend the returned user object to the list on HTTP 201.
rationale: Prepending the new user gives the admin immediate visual confirmation without a full list refresh.

title: Create user — HTTP 409 conflict handling
description: The admin frontend module shall display Username already exists. inline in the modal when POST /api/v1/users returns HTTP 409.
rationale: The handler returns 409 with error username already taken when a duplicate username is detected; this must surface as a human-readable inline error.

title: Create user modal — cancel closes without request
description: The admin frontend module shall close the create user modal and discard all field values when Cancel is clicked.
rationale: Cancelling must be a no-op; no partial data should be submitted to the server.

title: Create user modal — submit button disabled during request
description: The admin frontend module shall disable the Submit button while the POST /api/v1/users request is in flight.
rationale: Double-submitting the form would create duplicate users; disabling the button prevents this.

title: Edit user modal — PATCH request body
description: The admin frontend module shall send PATCH /api/v1/users/{id} with JSON body containing only the username and email fields.
rationale: The modifyUser handler accepts only username and email as patchable fields; including other fields has no effect but the body must match the expected shape.

title: Edit user — HTTP 200 success handling
description: The admin frontend module shall close the edit modal and update the user's list row in place on HTTP 200.
rationale: In-place update avoids a full list refresh and preserves the scroll position.

title: Edit user — HTTP 409 conflict handling
description: The admin frontend module shall display Username already exists. inline in the edit modal when PATCH /api/v1/users/{id} returns HTTP 409.
rationale: A renamed username may conflict with an existing account; the error must be shown in context.

title: Edit user modal — pre-fill current values
description: The admin frontend module shall populate the edit modal username and email fields from the user's current list row data.
rationale: Pre-filling prevents the admin from accidentally blanking a field they did not intend to change.

title: Edit user modal — submit button disabled during request
description: The admin frontend module shall disable the Save button while the PATCH /api/v1/users/{id} request is in flight.
rationale: Double-submitting would send two consecutive PATCH requests that could conflict with each other.

title: Deactivate — confirm dialog text
description: The admin frontend module shall confirm deactivation with the message Deactivate {username}? They will not be able to log in.
rationale: The confirmation message must name the specific user and state the consequence to prevent mistaken deactivation.

title: Deactivate — POST request
description: The admin frontend module shall send POST /api/v1/users/{id}/deactivate after the admin confirms the deactivation dialog.
rationale: The deactivateUser handler is registered at POST /{id}/deactivate in AdminRoutes.

title: Deactivate — HTTP 204 success handling
description: The admin frontend module shall mark the user inactive in the list when POST /api/v1/users/{id}/deactivate returns HTTP 204.
rationale: The deactivateUser handler returns 204 No Content on success; the list must reflect the new inactive status without a full refresh.

title: Deactivate — cancel dialog aborts request
description: The admin frontend module shall not issue the POST /api/v1/users/{id}/deactivate request when the admin dismisses the confirmation dialog.
rationale: Cancelling must be a no-op; no state change should occur.

title: Activate — POST request
description: The admin frontend module shall send POST /api/v1/users/{id}/activate without a confirmation dialog when the Activate button is clicked.
rationale: Activation restores access but is reversible; a confirmation step is not required and would add friction.

title: Activate — HTTP 204 success handling
description: The admin frontend module shall mark the user active in the list when POST /api/v1/users/{id}/activate returns HTTP 204.
rationale: The activateUser handler returns 204 No Content on success; the list must reflect the active status without a full refresh.

title: Delete — confirm dialog text
description: The admin frontend module shall confirm deletion with Permanently delete {username} and all their data? This cannot be undone.
rationale: Deletion is irreversible and cascades to all student data; the dialog must explicitly state the permanence to prevent accidental deletion.

title: Delete — DELETE request
description: The admin frontend module shall send DELETE /api/v1/users/{id} after the admin confirms the deletion dialog.
rationale: The deleteStudent handler is registered at DELETE /{id} in AdminRoutes.

title: Delete — HTTP 204 success handling
description: The admin frontend module shall remove the deleted user's row from the list when DELETE /api/v1/users/{id} returns HTTP 204.
rationale: The deleteStudent handler returns 204 No Content; the row must disappear from the list immediately.

title: Delete — HTTP 409 conflict handling
description: The admin frontend module shall display Cannot delete: student has an active course. when DELETE /api/v1/users/{id} returns HTTP 409.
rationale: The deleteStudent handler returns 409 with error agent operations could not be terminated when in-flight work blocks deletion; this must be surfaced clearly.

title: Delete — cancel dialog aborts request
description: The admin frontend module shall not issue the DELETE /api/v1/users/{id} request when the admin dismisses the deletion confirmation dialog.
rationale: Cancelling must be a no-op; no data must be deleted.

title: Audit list — GET request parameters
description: The admin frontend module shall send GET /api/v1/audit with no query parameters on mount.
rationale: The audit list handler defaults to limit=50; omitting the parameter on first load uses the server default.

title: Audit list — response shape
description: The admin frontend module shall read the entries array and next_before integer from the GET /api/v1/audit response body.
rationale: The audit list handler returns { entries: [...], next_before: int64 }; the frontend must parse both fields.

title: Audit list — entry_hash truncation
description: The admin frontend module shall display only the first eight characters of the entry_hash field for each audit entry.
rationale: Showing the full 64-character SHA-256 hex digest would make the table unreadable; truncation preserves recognisability.

title: Audit list — Load More sends before cursor
description: The admin frontend module shall send GET /api/v1/audit?before={next_before} when Load More is clicked, using the cursor from the previous response.
rationale: The audit handler uses the before query parameter as a cursor for keyset pagination over int64 IDs.

title: Audit list — Load More hidden when exhausted
description: The admin frontend module shall hide the Load More button when the next_before value returned by the server is zero.
rationale: A next_before of zero indicates no more entries exist; the button must not appear when there is nothing further to load.

title: Audit verify — GET request
description: The admin frontend module shall send GET /api/v1/audit/verify when the Verify Integrity button is clicked.
rationale: The verify handler streams all entries and recomputes the hash chain; this must be triggered explicitly by the admin.

title: Audit verify — valid=true success message
description: The admin frontend module shall display Audit log integrity verified. All {count} entries are intact. when valid=true.
rationale: A positive confirmation with the entry count gives the admin a complete picture of the verified chain.

title: Audit verify — valid=false warning message
description: The admin frontend module shall display WARNING: Audit log integrity check failed. Chain broken at entry {first_broken_id}. when valid=false.
rationale: The verify handler returns first_broken_id when the chain is broken; the admin must see the exact entry ID to investigate.

title: Audit verify — network or server error message
description: The admin frontend module shall display Verification failed. Please try again. when GET /api/v1/audit/verify fails.
rationale: Verification failures must not be silently swallowed; the admin must be prompted to retry.

title: Config field — agent_retry_limit
description: The admin frontend module shall render agent_retry_limit as a number input and reject values less than one before submission.
rationale: The backend validates agent_retry_limit as an integer >= 1; client-side enforcement matches that rule.

title: Config field — correction_loop_max_iterations
description: The admin frontend module shall render correction_loop_max_iterations as a number input and reject values less than one before submission.
rationale: The backend validates correction_loop_max_iterations as an integer >= 1.

title: Config field — per_student_token_limit
description: The admin frontend module shall render per_student_token_limit as a number input and reject values less than zero before submission.
rationale: The backend validates per_student_token_limit as an integer >= 0; zero disables the limit.

title: Config field — late_penalty_rate
description: The admin frontend module shall render late_penalty_rate as a number input and reject values outside 0.0 to 1.0 before submission.
rationale: The backend validates late_penalty_rate as a float between 0.0 and 1.0 inclusive.

title: Config field — homework_weight
description: The admin frontend module shall render homework_weight as a number input and reject non-positive or greater-than-one values.
rationale: The backend validates homework_weight as a float > 0.0 and <= 1.0.

title: Config field — project_weight
description: The admin frontend module shall render project_weight as a number input and reject non-positive or greater-than-one values.
rationale: The backend validates project_weight as a float > 0.0 and <= 1.0.

title: Config field — session_inactivity_seconds
description: The admin frontend module shall render session_inactivity_seconds as a number input and reject values less than one before submission.
rationale: The backend validates session_inactivity_seconds as an integer >= 1.

title: Config field — account_lockout_seconds
description: The admin frontend module shall render account_lockout_seconds as a number input and reject values less than one before submission.
rationale: The backend validates account_lockout_seconds as an integer >= 1.

title: Config field — max_upload_bytes
description: The admin frontend module shall render max_upload_bytes as a number input and reject values less than 1024 before submission.
rationale: The backend validates max_upload_bytes as an integer >= 1024.

title: Config field — content_generation_timeout_seconds
description: The admin frontend module shall render content_generation_timeout_seconds as a number input and reject values less than one before submission.
rationale: The backend validates content_generation_timeout_seconds as an integer >= 1.

title: Config field — audit_retention_days
description: The admin frontend module shall render audit_retention_days as a number input and reject values less than one before submission.
rationale: The backend validates audit_retention_days as an integer >= 1.

title: Config field — notification_retention_days
description: The admin frontend module shall render notification_retention_days as a number input and reject values less than one before submission.
rationale: The backend validates notification_retention_days as an integer >= 1.

title: Config field — consent_version
description: The admin frontend module shall render consent_version as a text input and reject an empty string before submission.
rationale: The backend validates consent_version as a non-empty string.

title: Config PATCH — request body shape
description: The admin frontend module shall send PATCH /api/v1/admin/config with a {"config":{}} body containing only the changed key-value pairs.
rationale: The patchConfig handler decodes a struct with a config map[string]string field; only changed keys are included to avoid redundant audit entries.

title: Config PATCH — all values sent as strings
description: The admin frontend module shall stringify all config values to strings before placing them in the PATCH request body.
rationale: The patchConfig handler accepts map[string]string; sending numeric types would cause a JSON decode error.

title: Config PATCH — Save button disabled during request
description: The admin frontend module shall disable the Save button while the PATCH /api/v1/admin/config request is in flight.
rationale: Double-submitting would send two concurrent PATCH requests that could interleave and produce inconsistent config state.

title: Unsaved changes indicator visibility
description: The admin frontend module shall display You have unsaved changes. when any config field value differs from its fetched value.
rationale: The indicator must appear on the first keystroke so the admin always knows whether the current form state has been persisted.

title: Config save success banner text
description: The admin frontend module shall display Configuration saved. and clear the unsaved indicator when the config PATCH returns HTTP 200.
rationale: The banner confirms the save and the cleared indicator reflects that the form now matches the persisted state.

title: Config server validation error display
description: The admin frontend module shall render each validation_errors string beneath the form field whose key prefixes that error string.
rationale: The patchConfig handler prefixes each validation error with the key name followed by a colon, e.g. homework_weight: ...; the frontend must parse this prefix to attach the error to the correct field.

title: Config client validation — weight sum must equal 1.0
description: The admin frontend module shall flag both weight fields when homework_weight plus project_weight does not equal 1.0 within 0.001.
rationale: The patchConfig handler enforces a cross-field weight sum rule; replicating it client-side prevents a server round-trip for this common constraint.

title: Config client validation — agent_retry_limit error message
description: The admin frontend module shall display agent_retry_limit must be an integer >= 1. when agent_retry_limit is not a positive integer.
rationale: Error text must match the backend message so instructions are consistent across the UI and API.

title: Config client validation — correction_loop_max_iterations error message
description: The admin frontend module shall show correction_loop_max_iterations must be an integer >= 1. when that field is not valid.
rationale: Error text must match the backend message.

title: Config client validation — per_student_token_limit error message
description: The admin frontend module shall display per_student_token_limit must be an integer >= 0. when per_student_token_limit is negative or non-integer.
rationale: Error text must match the backend message.

title: Config client validation — late_penalty_rate error message
description: The admin frontend module shall show late_penalty_rate must be a float between 0.0 and 1.0 inclusive. when invalid.
rationale: Error text must match the backend message.

title: Config client validation — homework_weight error message
description: The admin frontend module shall show homework_weight must be a float > 0.0 and <= 1.0. when homework_weight is invalid.
rationale: Error text must match the backend message.

title: Config client validation — project_weight error message
description: The admin frontend module shall show project_weight must be a float > 0.0 and <= 1.0. when project_weight is invalid.
rationale: Error text must match the backend message.

title: Config client validation — session_inactivity_seconds error message
description: The admin frontend module shall show session_inactivity_seconds must be an integer >= 1. when session_inactivity_seconds is invalid.
rationale: Error text must match the backend message.

title: Config client validation — account_lockout_seconds error message
description: The admin frontend module shall show account_lockout_seconds must be an integer >= 1. when account_lockout_seconds is invalid.
rationale: Error text must match the backend message.

title: Config client validation — max_upload_bytes error message
description: The admin frontend module shall show max_upload_bytes must be an integer >= 1024. when max_upload_bytes is invalid.
rationale: Error text must match the backend message.

title: Config client validation — content_generation_timeout_seconds error message
description: The admin frontend module shall show content_generation_timeout_seconds must be an integer >= 1. when that field is invalid.
rationale: Error text must match the backend message.

title: Config client validation — audit_retention_days error message
description: The admin frontend module shall show audit_retention_days must be an integer >= 1. when audit_retention_days is invalid.
rationale: Error text must match the backend message.

title: Config client validation — notification_retention_days error message
description: The admin frontend module shall show notification_retention_days must be an integer >= 1. when that field is invalid.
rationale: Error text must match the backend message.

title: Config client validation — consent_version error message
description: The admin frontend module shall display consent_version must be a non-empty string. when the field value is empty.
rationale: Error text must match the backend message.

title: Course oversight — GET request
description: The admin frontend module shall send GET /api/v1/courses?limit=20 on mount to fetch the first page of all system-wide courses.
rationale: The listCourses handler returns all courses for admin role callers; the default limit of 20 is used for the initial load.

title: Course oversight — response shape
description: The admin frontend module shall read the courses array and next_cursor string from the GET /api/v1/courses response body.
rationale: The listCourses handler returns { courses: [...], next_cursor: string }; the frontend must parse both fields.

title: Course oversight — no action buttons rendered
description: The admin frontend module shall render no action buttons for any course row in the course oversight view.
rationale: The course oversight view is read-only; admins must not be able to mutate course state from this view.

title: Course oversight status dropdown options
description: The admin frontend module shall provide all, intake, syllabus_draft, syllabus_approved, generating, active, archived, and completed in the status dropdown.
rationale: These are the only valid status values accepted by the listCourses handler's status query parameter.

title: Course oversight status filter — request
description: The admin frontend module shall send GET /api/v1/courses?status={value} and replace the course list when the status dropdown changes.
rationale: Changing the filter must reload the list from the start so the cursor is reset; appending to the old list would mix statuses.

title: Course oversight — Load More sends cursor
description: The admin frontend module shall send GET /api/v1/courses?cursor={next_cursor} when Load More is clicked, preserving any active status filter.
rationale: The listCourses handler uses the cursor query parameter for keyset pagination; the status filter must be preserved across pages.

title: Course oversight — Load More hidden when exhausted
description: The admin frontend module shall hide the Load More button when the server returns an empty next_cursor string.
rationale: An empty next_cursor indicates no further courses exist for the current filter; the button must not appear.

title: Audit table — actor username column
description: The admin frontend module shall render the actor_username field in a dedicated column for each audit entry.
rationale: The actor_username is the human-readable identifier for the admin who performed the action; displaying it makes the log immediately readable without cross-referencing user IDs.

title: Audit table — formatted timestamp column
description: The admin frontend module shall render the created_at field as a locale-formatted date-time string in each audit row.
rationale: Raw ISO 8601 timestamps are hard to read at a glance; a locale date-time format reduces cognitive effort when scanning the audit log.

title: Audit table — action column
description: The admin frontend module shall render the action field in a dedicated column for each audit entry.
rationale: The action field names the specific operation that was performed, which is the central fact an admin needs when reviewing the log.

title: Audit table — target column
description: The admin frontend module shall render target_type and target_id in a combined target column per audit row.
rationale: Combining target_type and target_id in one column gives admins the object identity without consuming two table columns.

title: Audit view — loading state on initial fetch
description: The admin frontend module shall display a loading indicator while the initial audit log fetch is in progress.
rationale: Large audit logs take time to retrieve; a loading state prevents the admin from thinking the view is broken during fetch.

title: Audit view — error state display
description: The admin frontend module shall display an error message when the audit log fetch returns a non-200 response.
rationale: Audit fetch failures must be visible so the admin knows the log could not be loaded rather than seeing an empty table.

title: Audit view — empty state display
description: The admin frontend module shall display No audit log entries found. when the server returns zero entries.
rationale: An explicit empty state tells the admin there are genuinely no entries rather than implying a loading or fetch error.

title: Audit Load More — disabled during in-flight request
description: The admin frontend module shall disable the Load More button while an audit fetch is in progress.
rationale: Clicking Load More while a fetch is already in flight would issue a second overlapping request that could interleave or duplicate entries.

title: Audit Load More — appends entries to existing list
description: The admin frontend module shall append entries from Load More responses to the existing entry list.
rationale: Replacing the list on Load More would discard already-loaded entries; appending preserves the full displayed history.

title: Audit table — one row per entry
description: The admin frontend module shall render exactly one table row for each audit entry returned by the server.
rationale: A one-to-one mapping between server entries and rendered rows ensures no entries are silently dropped or duplicated in the display.

title: User list row — email column
description: The admin frontend module shall render the email field from each user object in a dedicated table column.
rationale: Email is an optional but commonly populated contact field; exposing it in the list lets admins verify account details without opening an edit modal.

title: Error banner dismiss button
description: The admin frontend module shall hide the error banner when the admin clicks the Dismiss button.
rationale: Errors that have been acknowledged must be dismissible so the admin can continue working without a persistent obstruction.

title: Config Fields Render With Persisted Values
description: The admin module shall render all system configuration fields populated with their current persisted values.
rationale: Administrators must see the live configuration state before editing; blank or stale fields would cause unintentional overwrites.

title: Config Change Persists After Reload
description: The admin module shall persist a saved configuration change so it is visible after a full page reload.
rationale: Saving a value that reverts on reload gives a false sense of success; administrators need durable changes to trust the configuration workflow.

title: Weight Sum Validation Blocks Save
description: The admin module shall block saving and display an error when grading weight values do not sum to 1.0.
rationale: Grading weights that do not sum to 1.0 would produce incorrect final grades; client-side validation prevents a wasted round-trip and immediate misconfiguration.

title: Secrets section renders on admin config page
description: The admin frontend module shall render a secrets section above the configuration fields on the system config view.
rationale: Managed secrets are a distinct credential concern from numeric configuration keys; placing the secrets section first on the config page makes their priority visible to admins.

title: Anthropic API key entry field is password-type and write-only
description: The admin frontend module shall render the Anthropic API key entry as a password-type input, never pre-filled.
rationale: A password-type input masks keystrokes from shoulder-surfing; never pre-filling ensures the stored credential is not transmitted back to the browser where it could be exfiltrated.

title: Brave Search API key entry field is password-type and write-only
description: The admin frontend module shall render the Brave Search API key entry as a password-type input, never pre-filled.
rationale: A password-type input masks keystrokes from shoulder-surfing; never pre-filling ensures the stored credential is not transmitted back to the browser where it could be exfiltrated.

title: Secret configured badge shows last-4 characters for managed secrets only
description: The admin frontend module shall display the last four characters of a managed secret value in the status badge.
rationale: Showing the last four characters gives the admin enough context to confirm which credential is active without exposing the full secret in the browser.

title: Clear button removes managed secret with confirmation dialog
description: The admin frontend module shall display a Clear button only for managed secrets and require a confirmation dialog before deletion.
rationale: Clearing a managed secret reverts the system to its environment-variable fallback; a confirmation step prevents accidental credential removal that would interrupt AI features.

title: Explanation blocks render for all 15 config and secret keys
description: The admin frontend module shall render an explanation block for each of the fifteen configuration and secret keys.
rationale: Configuration keys have non-obvious consequences; an always-available explanation block lets admins understand the impact of a change without consulting external documentation.

title: Reserved-key explanations disclose env-override behaviour honestly
description: The admin frontend module shall label reserved configuration keys as having no effect on the running server.
rationale: Admins who change a reserved key expect it to take effect immediately; honest labeling prevents wasted troubleshooting time and protects against false assurance of a security configuration change.

title: Inert-key explanations disclose missing purge worker for audit_retention_days
description: The admin frontend module shall disclose in the audit_retention_days explanation that no automated purge worker is implemented.
rationale: Without this disclosure an admin setting audit_retention_days would believe aged entries are being deleted; the honest label prevents a false compliance expectation.

title: Agent and generation key explanations accurate to implementation
description: The admin frontend module shall state the consequence of changing each agent and content-generation configuration key in its explanation.
rationale: Agent and generation parameters directly affect student wait times and AI cost; admins must understand the operational trade-off before adjusting any of these keys.

title: Grading key explanations accurate to implementation
description: The admin frontend module shall state the consequence of changing each grading configuration key in its explanation.
rationale: Grading keys directly affect student scores and course outcomes; incorrect or absent explanations could lead to misconfiguration that harms students' grades.

title: Session and security key explanations accurate to implementation
description: The admin frontend module shall identify the effective source for each session and security configuration key in its explanation.
rationale: Session and security keys have mixed effectiveness: some are wired to live state, others are reserved for future use; admins must know which keys actually govern runtime behaviour.

title: Managed-secret key explanations describe resolution order accurately
description: The admin frontend module shall state in each managed-secret explanation that a managed value takes precedence over the environment variable.
rationale: The resolution order (managed secret beats env var) is a non-obvious system property; an explanation stating this order prevents confusion when both sources are set simultaneously.
